Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

someday adverb

at some time in the future

also some day, one day (in the future), one of these days, sometime, at some point

classical

Cic. Fam. 14.4: huic utinam aliquandō grātiam referre possīmus! (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Mil. 69: illūcēscet aliquandō ille diēs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 88

aliquandō

Wiktionary

some day, at some time

An indefinite time, past, present or future; in a negative or doubtful clause “ever” is umquam.

Other words

  • ōlim — one day, hereafter

    also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.203: forsan et haec ōlim meminisse juvābit · Wiktionary

    Usually “once, long ago” (see once upon a time); of the future, Lewis & Short call it rare but classical.

Examples

  • forsan et haec ōlim meminisse juvābit

    perhaps one day it will be a joy to remember even thisVerg. A. 1.203

See also sometimes, ever, once upon a time, future.
